text:
Wyatt Johnston is the most obvious case on our board of a player whose goal total lies about him. He has 3 goals on 8.3 expected, shooting 7.3% when his talent range sits around 14 to 18%. Last season he scored 45. Chances like these don't usually stay unconverted.

The rest of his game has carried on regardless. He has 16 points in 15 games, 9 on the power play, a five-game point streak built on assists, and Dallas gets 56% of the expected goals at five on five with him on, seven points better than without him. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking put his home-plate chances in the 93rd percentile last season, and he's still getting there.

The flip side from Evolving-Hockey: last season he was also better than his goals (2.5 expected wins against 0.9 actual), and opponents generated more with him on the ice than with most forwards. So the finishing has lagged for a while now, and there's a defensive cost. Watch the slot: the chances are there. When they start going in, the line moves from good to scary.
headline: Wyatt Johnston keeps getting the looks
